metas.name: 120-Degree Angle
metas.note:
These attachments with an approximately 120-degree angle can commonly be found on poles in Kansai.

NOTE: Sometimes there is no angle, and instead just an angled downward attachment.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: 90-Degree Angle
metas.note: These smaller attachments with a 90-degree angle can commonly be found on poles in Shikoku.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Aichi Road Diamond
metas.note:
You can narrow down the prefecture you are in based on the style of road diamond.

Aichi uses a regular but thin design
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Akita Bollard
metas.note: This bollard, much like Tohoku, will be a thick, white bollard with an octagonal reflector. However, this Akita prefecture variation will have two yellow stripes underneath the reflector.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Aomori Bollard
metas.note: This bollard, found in the Aomori prefecture, has two yellow stripes, a single circular reflector, and is extendable. Sometimes, only one thicker stripe near the top may be present.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Aomori Road Diamond
metas.note:
You can narrow down the prefecture you are in based on the style of road diamond.

This design can only be found in Aomori.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Aomori Signpost Sticker
metas.note: Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Bamboo
metas.note: In general, bamboo grows more often in the south, and slowly decreases further north. Population size and areas where it grows can vary, so use this information primarily in helping assist your region guess.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Birch-painted Pole
metas.note: These artistically painted poles, made to resemble birch trees, are unique to the city of Date in Hokkaido.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Cabbage
metas.note:
Cabbage is abundant in Hokkaido and some northern prefectures. Plants found south of Hokkaido often have smaller leaves. It is often found growing along the roadside.

NOTE: Cabbage is also found on the island of Sakhalin, Russia. However, the Google car will not have low-cam there.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Chevron-like/Orange Sticker
metas.note:
You can find these chevron-like stickers, or more rarely orange ones, on guardrails in Hokkaido.

On the end or side of a guardrail.

Stuck to metal posts between wire fences, which are often found in Hokkaido.

On railings, which are often found on bridges, underneath the inside of the railing.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Chinese Silver Grass
metas.note:
Chinese Silver Grass, referred to as Kyushu grass, is indeed very abundant on the island of Kyushu. However, use this tip with caution, as they can be seen outside of this area.

NOTE: Another notable region they can be found in is the prefectures of Niigata, Yamagata and Akita. Though, combining the rather large quantity found on Kyushu, its normally distinct vegetation, along with other information, there often will be a clear distinction.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Chubu Pole
metas.note: The transformers in Chubu, which often have painted yellow numbers and black “tap” connectors, are either attached with large triangle and horizontal bars, or these thin metal brackets.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Chubu Pole Plate
metas.note:
Every region in Japan features a distinct plate on their utility poles.

The Chubu pole plate is the only pole plate with rounded edges/rounded shape.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Chubu Pole Reflector
metas.note: The pole reflector pads vary by region in Japan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Chubu Pole Top (1)
metas.note: This pole top, with four thicker bars and a circle piece at the top, is common in the Chubu region.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Chubu Pole Top (2)
metas.note: This tuning fork pole top, with a short top bar and horizontal bar below, is found the majority of the time in the Chubu region.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Chubu/Okinawa Guy Wire
metas.note:
Most regions in Japan have unique guy wires.

NOTE: Only the most consistent ones are on this map.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Chugoku Guy Wire
metas.note:
Most regions in Japan have unique guy wires.

NOTE: Only the most consistent ones are on this map.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Chugoku Pole
metas.note:
The transformers in Chugoku, which have a cross-shaped bar attached in the middle of the pole, mounted by a full triangle, will have a long horizontal or short vertical insulator(s) at the end.

A white sticker will often be stuck to the bottom of the transformer with red numbers. They may also be painted on the side.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Chugoku Pole Plate
metas.note:
Every region in Japan features a distinct plate on their utility poles.

The pole plates in Chugoku have always "Energia" written in latin on them.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Chugoku Pole Reflector
metas.note: The pole reflector pads vary by region in Japan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Chugoku Pole Top
metas.note: This pole top, with four thin, skinny bars, is common in the Chugoku region.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Claymore
metas.note: Kerosine tanks, otherwise known as “Claymores”, can be found more commonly the further north you go. They are abundant in Hokkaido, but can be found in prefectures south of it, or in high elevation mountainous areas.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Cycling Route
metas.note:
Cycling routes in Ehime use an outside white, with an inside blue line. They are more commonly found along the coast but may be found further inland too.

While exceptions do exist, and can be found in other prefectures, they are the extreme minority.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Cyrillic Letters
metas.note: Cyrillic can be found on signs in the cities of Wakkanai and Nemuro, in northern Hokkaido.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Ehime Signpost Sticker
metas.note: Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Fukuoka Signpost Sticker
metas.note: Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Gas Tank
metas.note: Hot water, gas and propane tanks can be found more frequently in northern prefectures or high elevation mountainous areas.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Gifu Road Diamond
metas.note:
You can narrow down the prefecture you are in based on the style of road diamond.

This design can also be found in Gunma, Chiba and as a thinner version in Yamanashi.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Gifu Signpost Sticker
metas.note: Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Green Band
metas.note: Green bands on guardrails are most commonly found in Oita and Miyazaki, but can be found on all of Kyushu.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Green Tea
metas.note:
Green tea plants are often grown in hedged rows. You will often see these fans mounted on poles, which serve the purpose of preventing frost from falling on the plants.

The prefectures of Shizuoka (36%) and Kagoshima (34%) make up the majority of the production, with Mie (7%), Miyazaki (4%), and other prefectures (17%) making up the minority.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Grey "Insulator-Esque" Blocks
metas.note: These grey “insulator-esque” blocks, which wires are fed through, can be found in the regions of Chubu, Kansai, Chugoku, Shikoku, and very rarely in Hokkaido.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Hokkaido Pole
metas.note:
The electrical poles in Hokkaido either have this plus-shaped bar attached to the side of the pole, or one transformer mounted on two bars.

However, if there is more than one transformer, they will often be mounted on the sides of a square.

NOTE: While the Kanto transformer may also be mounted on two bars, Hokkaido will never have a wooden plate.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Hokkaido Pole Plate
metas.note:
Every region in Japan features a distinct plate on their utility poles.

The Hokkaido pole plate is the plate with the highest amount of characters on one plate.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Hokkaido Signpost Sticker
metas.note: Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Hokuriku Pole
metas.note:
The transformers in Hokuriku, which are attached with thin metal bars, often have these small “lamp” shaped insulators. There will never be a bar present except for the attachment mentioned above.

NOTE: The prefecture of Niigata will have the Tohoku transformer design, as opposed to Hokuriku one.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Hokuriku Pole Plate
metas.note:
Every region in Japan features a distinct plate on their utility poles.

There are multiple horizontal plates attached to the poles in Hokuriku. They are including NTT
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Hokuriku Pole Reflector
metas.note: The pole reflector pads vary by region in Japan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Hokuriku Pole Top
metas.note: This pole top, with two sides filled in and shaped like a tent, is common in the Hokuriku region.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Hyogo Signpost Sticker
metas.note: Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Ibaraki Signpost Sticker
metas.note: Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Infrastructural Arrow (Highway 275)
metas.note:
This infrastructural arrow informs drivers of where the shoulder line is when under snow, and is located almost exclusively in Hokkaido.

This alternate yellow and black design can often be found on the northern part of National Highway 275 in Hokkaido.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Infrastructural Arrow (Long)
metas.note:
This infrastructural arrow informs drivers of where the shoulder line is when under snow, and is located almost exclusively in Hokkaido.

This variation, found in the Gifu prefecture, is long and thin.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Infrastructural Arrow (normal)
metas.note: This infrastructural arrow informs drivers of where the shoulder line is when under snow, and is located almost exclusively in Hokkaido.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Infrastructural Arrow (Silver Bolts)
metas.note:
This infrastructural arrow informs drivers of where the shoulder line is when under snow, and is located almost exclusively in Hokkaido.

This arrow, found in the Aomori prefecture (or more rarely Hokkaido), has distinct silver bolts around the border.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Infrastructural Arrow (Yellow/Black)
metas.note:
This infrastructural arrow informs drivers of where the shoulder line is when under snow, and is located almost exclusively in Hokkaido.

This yellow and black arrow can be found on Hokkaido.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Infrastructural Arrow (Yellow/Green)
metas.note:
This infrastructural arrow informs drivers of where the shoulder line is when under snow, and is located almost exclusively in Hokkaido.

This yellow and green arrow is found southwest of Sapporo.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Japanese White Birch
metas.note:
Japanese White Birch grows dominantly in the Chubu and Hokkaido regions, and to a lesser extent in Tohoku. Small areas of white birch can be found throughout Japan, so use this information primarily to help assist your region guess.

NOTE: Japanese Beech is another species of tree found in Japan. They, however, have more grey and spotted bark, as opposed to the mostly white Japanese White Birch.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Kagawa Road Diamond
metas.note: You can narrow down the prefecture you are in based on the style of road diamond.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Kagawa Sign
metas.note: These specific black signs with two yellow circles are found in Kagawa. Other variations can be seen, including them stacked on top of each other, or with an arrow attached above.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Kanagawa Signpost Sticker
metas.note: Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Kansai Pole
metas.note:
The transformers in Kansai have either a straight or zigzag bar mounted on the bottom of a square. The transformer(s) will be mounted on the sides of that same square.

While this is uncommon, the bar and transformer(s) may be mounted on a vertical bar, rather than a square.

NOTE: While Tohoku may have a square attachment as well, the bar will be mounted on the top rather than the bottom.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Kansai Pole Plate
metas.note:
Every region in Japan features a distinct plate on their utility poles.

This plate can be recognized by the Japanese written vertically in the middle/ on the right with other characters written in rows of two. In the bottom left and right corner are also other characters written.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Kansai Pole Reflector
metas.note: The pole reflector pads vary by region in Japan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Kansai Pole Top
metas.note: This tuning fork pole top, with a thin wire and horizontal bar below, is common in the Kansai region.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Kansai/Hokuriku/Shikoku Guy Wire
metas.note:
Most regions in Japan have unique guy wires.

NOTE: Only the most consistent ones are on this map.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Kanto Pole
metas.note:
The transformers in Kanto, which can have three or two insulators, are often mounted on a wooden plate and two bars, or a round plate and a T-shaped bar.

NOTE: While the Hokkaido transformer may also be mounted on two bars, Tokyo will always have a wooden plate.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Kanto Pole Plate
metas.note: Every region in Japan features a distinct plate on their utility poles.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Kanto Pole Top
metas.note: This tuning fork pole top, with a long top bar that sticks out each end and horizontal bar(s) below, is found the majority of the time in the Kanto region.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Kumamoto Signpost Sticker
metas.note:
Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.

These sticker in the prefecture of Kumamoto can also be found in Kagoshima and Miyazaki (In Kagoshima and Miyazaki, they can have changed colors)
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Kyushu Pole
metas.note: The transformers in Kyushu, which have a straight bar attached on the side of the pole with three insulators at the end, will have transformers mounted 180-degrees from one another.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Kyushu Pole Platew
metas.note:
Every region in Japan features a distinct plate on their utility poles.

The Kyushu plate has a small logo on top, under the logo there are 3 numbers written horizontally and then 4 characters written vertically on the right.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Kyushu/Okinawa Guy Wire
metas.note:
Most regions in Japan have unique guy wires.

NOTE: Only the most consistent ones are on this map.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Kyushu/Okinawa Pole Reflector
metas.note: The pole reflector pads vary by region in Japan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Kyushu/Yamaguchi Bollard
metas.note:
This flat, white bollard, found on the island of Kyushu and in Yamaguchi Prefecture, will have a series of separated orange reflectors on one side, and the same white on the opposite.

NOTE: Rarely, you may find similar bollards in Hokkaido. However, both sides will have orange reflectors.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Manhole Design
metas.note: Tokyo City features a nice manhole design, with a 5 petal flower and many small circles on the outside.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Mie Road Diamond
metas.note:
You can narrow down the prefecture you are in based on the style of road diamond.

This road diamond can also be found in the Kochi prefecture. In the Kumamoto and Ishikawa prefecture it is the same design, but in a thinner version.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Miyagi Road Diamond
metas.note:
You can narrow down the prefecture you are in based on the style of road diamond.

This road diamond can also be found in the Kyoto, Hyogo and Okayama prefecture. In the Tokushima and Hiroshima prefecture it is the same design, but in a smaller version.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Miyagi Signpost Sticker
metas.note: Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Nagano Signpost Sticker
metas.note: Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Nagasaki Signpost Sticker
metas.note:
Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.

This design can also be found in the Saga prefectur.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Nara Signpost Sticker
metas.note: Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Northern House
metas.note:
The further you are north, roofs generally transition from tiled to level or flat sloped in order to compensate for heavy snowfall. Northern houses often have ladders attached to the side, giving roof access to clear snow.

NOTE: In addition to north to south, high-elevation mountainous regions or high snowfall areas often use such roofs, even in more central or southern prefectures.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Oita Signpost Sticker
metas.note: Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Okayama Bollard
metas.note: This bollard, with an octagonal reflector, and red stripe underneath it, is exclusive to the Okayama prefecture. Additionally, there will be a sloped connection where the base meets the reflector.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Okayama Signpost Sticker
metas.note: Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Okinawa House
metas.note: Okinawa can often be recognised by the white concrete buildings with flat roofs.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Okinawa Pole
metas.note: Transformers in Okinawa, which have a T-shaped bar attached on the side of the pole, will have transformers mounted on opposite sides of the pole.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Okinawa Pole Plate
metas.note: Every region in Japan features a distinct plate on their utility poles.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Orange and Black Band
metas.note: These orange and black bands wrapped around poles can often be found in Shikoku.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Orange Arrow
metas.note: You may sometimes find an orange arrow located above the top most pole plate in Chugoku.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Osaka Signpost Sticker
metas.note: Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Plains
metas.note:
Japan is notably a very mountainous country. However, there are some regions that are quite flat, being the Nobi and Kanto plains. While at times they can look very similar, determining that it is one or the other can be very helpful.

NOTE: While there are, of course, other flat areas in Japan, these two are the most recognizable.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Red Field
metas.note: Agricultural fields with red soil are commonly found on several southern islands, most notably on the islands of Miyakojima and Ishigaki in southern Okinawa.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Red-Tiled Roof
metas.note: These unique red-tiled roofs are most commonly found in Chugoku, especially in the prefectures of Hiroshima and Shimane.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Red/Yellow Sticker
metas.note: Guardrail endings with these red and yellow striped stickers can commonly be found across Chugoku, except in Yamaguchi. They can also rarely be found in Niigata.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Rice
metas.note:
Rice is mainly produced north of Tokyo. During growth, it resembles straws of grass. And when ready for harvest, brown husks are visible. They are also commonly planted in beds of water.

The regions of Chubu (21%), Kanto (15%), Tohoku (27%), and Hokkaido (7%) make up the majority of production.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Shikoku Bollard
metas.note: Some bollards on the island of Shikoku can have a black stripe just under the reflector. They can be found normally, attached to guardrails or walls.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Shikoku Pole
metas.note:
The transformers in Shikoku, which also have a cross-shaped bar attached in the middle of the pole, mounted by a half triangle, will have “hat shaped” short horizontal insulators at the end.

A white sticker will often be stuck to the bottom of the transformer with black numbers.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Shikoku Pole Plate
metas.note:
Every region in Japan features a distinct plate on their utility poles.

The Shikoku pole plate can be recognized by the "4-squares"-Logo, that stands for the 4 prefectures on the island of Shikoku and the multiple rows of characters from left to right below.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Shikoku Pole Reflector
metas.note: The pole reflector pads vary by region in Japan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Shimane Signpost Sticker
metas.note:
Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.

The color of the band can vary in this prefectur.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Shisa
metas.note: You can find these ‘Shisa’ guardian lions and house plaques with these specific characters in Okinawa. The colour and shapes of both can vary.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Shizuoka Road Diamond
metas.note: You can narrow down the prefecture you are in based on the style of road diamond.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Shizuoka Signpost Sticker
metas.note: Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Snow Poles
metas.note: In the northern parts of the Chugoku region, you can primarily find these basic snow poles, with either a thin extended, or thin contracted top. They can also sometimes be found in Iwate.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Snow Prevention Road
metas.note: Snow prevention roads, known as ‘Shosetsu’, are found mainly in northwest coastal prefectures. They appear as tiny circles in the pavement, and spray warm underground water to clear snow.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Striped Bollard
metas.note: These striped bollards (which cover over the original) have a thinner top half, and no reflectors, and are common to the Tohoku region. They are especially common in Akita prefecture.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Sugarcane
metas.note: Sugarcane is almost exclusively found on the islands in southern Kyushu and Okinawa.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Tochigi Road Diamond
metas.note:
You can narrow down the prefecture you are in based on the style of road diamond.

This design can also be found in the Ibaraki, Saitama and Niigata prefectur.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Tohoku Bollard
metas.note:
This thick, white bollard, found in the Tohoku region, will have an octagonal reflector, and yellow stripe just underneath. In addition, you can find the same bollard, but with a rectangular top.

Finally, there are two other variations. You can find a black octagonal, and rectangular version. They are often found on National Highways or Expressways and can have the number printed on them.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Tohoku Pole
metas.note:
The transformers in Tohoku, which often have additional square holding brackets and the logo of the Tohoku Electrical Company, are sometimes mounted on a round plate with a zigzag bar.

Furthermore, you may also find transformers mounted on the side of a square, with a straight bar mounted on the top of the square. Rarely, you may find a square without a bar.

NOTE: While Kansai may have a square attachment as well, the bar will be mounted on the bottom rather than the top.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Tohoku Pole Plate
metas.note:
Every region in Japan features a distinct plate on their utility poles.

The Tohoku pole plates can be recognized by the fact, that one plate is vertical and longer and the other plate is silver, short and horizontally.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Toyama Bollard
metas.note:
The Toyama prefecture bollard has one reflector, is extendable and has a red stripe underneath the reflector.

NOTE: Be careful: if there is either a second reflector, or a yellow stripe instead of a red one, these are different bollards. These are more common variations found across many prefectures.

metas.note: Vertical traffic lights can be found in Hokkaido, and along the northwestern coast. The usual horizontal traffic lights can be found everywhere else.
